To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) channel estimation is controlled by an effective SNR, the product of the pilot signal SNR and the coherence time; (ii) the receiver performance is controlled jointly by the coherence time, the pilot signal SNRs, and the Doppler spread; and (iii) the receiver performance can be significantly improved by exploiting the joint multipath-DOPPLER diversity.

the normalized coherence time is a key parameter that determines the performance of a pilot-based channel estimation scheme for coherent CDMA systems, and that exploiting joint multipath-Dopper diversity can significantly mitigate error probability floors in fast fading channels.

(i) the performance of linear MMSE channel estimators is characterized by an "effective pilot SNR", which is the product of the pilot power and the normalized coherence-time of the channel, (ii) a simple uniform averaging estimator achieves near-optimal performance and is easy to implement if the effective pilot SNR is sufficiently large, and (iii) exploiting joint multipath-DOPPLER diversity can significantly mitigate performance floors due to imperfect channel estimation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient pilot-assisted receivers that are robust to time-varying fading and can operate reliably in a variety of channel environments.
the design of coherent CDMA systems that are robust to errors in channel estimates, which is a key requirement for practical systems.
the fundamental limits of coherent CDMA receivers in fast-fading multipath channels, and with the design of practical channel estimation and coherent receivers.

coherent CDMA receivers with Doppler diversity can achieve near-optimal performance under severe fading conditions, provided that the channel is estimated accurately.
, for a given pilot SNR, the overall receiver performance improves with the normalized coherence time until a certain point, after which the performance starts to degrade.
, in a fast-fading environment, the coherent receiver performance is controlled jointly by the normalized coherence time and the pilot SNR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coherent receiver performance is controlled not only by the pilot SNR, but also by the normalized coherence time and the number of multipath components.
the performance of coherent Rake receivers is determined by two key channel characteristics: the normalized coherence time and the normalized Doppler spread.
the coherent receiver performance is controlled primarily by the normalized coherence time and is only secondarily affected by channel estimation errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
channel estimation and coherent receiver design should jointly account for the Doppler diversity available in the system.
the normalized coherence time is the most critical parameter controlling system performance.
channel estimation and coherent receiver design should be jointly considered in the context of time-vary multipath channels.
